neighbours.label: The name of a drug class or prescribed medicine in a treatment context (triptans, nitrates, insulin, bronchodilators), vs the same treatment frame with a non-drug noun
fire: For severe attacks, her neurologist switched her to a different triptan.
The cardiologist added long-acting nitrates to control his angina.
Type 1 diabetics need to inject insulin several times a day.
During a flare, the patient inhaled a bronchodilator every four hours.
Many people with high blood pressure take beta blockers each morning.
Her doctor warned that combining antidepressants with triptans can be risky.
After the heart attack he was prescribed statins and aspirin.
The child with asthma carries inhaled corticosteroids to school.
quiet: For severe attacks, her neurologist switched her to a different schedule.
The cardiologist added long daily walks to control his weight.
Type 1 diabetics need to check their feet several times a day.
During a flare, the patient rested in a dark room every four hours.
Many people with high blood pressure take a short walk each morning.
Her doctor warned that combining late nights with stress can be risky.
After the heart attack he was given a booklet and a diet plan.
